doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Playing with Sun Ra and the Arkestra
summary: He played with Sun Ra in Chicago and New York and recalls Marshall Allen, Gilmore and Boykins and Sun Ra's space themes.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah. A wonderful chart. How about Sun Ra? Did you have an interaction with him early on?

Yeah. I played with him a lot in Chicago with the Arkestra and then after I came to New York, he came after that. And I played some gigs with him in New York too. So Sun Ra was like an enigma. You know he talked about space a lot. I think when the synthesizers came out he loved that, because he was always hearing some space stuff. But he was a, dare I say a phenomena in the fact that right now the Arkestra is still going on, led by 100-year-old — oh what’s his name?

Marshall Allen. Yeah. I played with Marshall back then. You know? And Ronnie Boykins, John Gilmore. So yeah it was definitely fun and definitely I found Sun Ra very interesting. He used to read sci-fi comic books and he definitely believed he was from Saturn. So I think some of that was ahead of his time in a way, some of the pieces he wrote. The interplanetary music. And so yeah, he still sustains today. I’m glad that I was part of some of that.
There’s probably albums with — actually we have a Sun Ra collection here at Hamilton and he seemed to record constantly.
Yup. He liked to keep a musical record of what he was doing. And so, and he had benefactors that, you know, made it possible for his music to be made public.
